title: Shopping Safely Online
drDigitalIntro:
Before you enter any payment details on a shopping site, take 5 seconds to check two things.
• Look at the address bar: a padlock icon means the connection is encrypted. No padlock, or a warning icon, means your data could be intercepted.
• Check the URL itself: the domain should be a name you recognize (like shop.example), not a jumbled mix of letters and numbers.
• Never type your card number into a site without a padlock — move on and find the official shop instead.
• A deal that seems too good to be true usually is — search the shop name plus the word 'reviews' before buying.
• For extra protection, use a credit card rather than a debit card: most banks offer fraud protection on purchases.

steps.say: Navigate to shop.example — a legitimate online store.
Click the padlock icon in the address bar to check this site's security.
Click the lock icon again — notice it says Not Secure.

drDigitalSuccess: A padlock, and an address you actually recognize, before you type a card number. The padlock on its own is not enough, which is why you read the address too.
drDigitalHint: Navigate to each site, then click the padlock (or warning icon) in the address bar to see its security status.
